sections.title: Why this work matters
sections.body: Northstar Health's patient access experience — scheduling, consent, and identity verification — has grown inconsistent across the health system's hospitals, employed-physician group, and ambulatory sites. Patients re-enter the same consent information at every touchpoint, and staff work around three different identity-verification processes depending on the site.

findings.theme: Consent capture is fragmented across sites
findings.evidence: Each site collects and stores patient consent differently; there is no single source of truth for what a patient has and hasn't authorized.
findings.implication: This creates both a patient-experience problem and a HIPAA documentation risk — Northstar cannot always demonstrate a consistent, current consent record on request.

findings.evidence: Ambulatory sites use a manual front-desk process; the employed-physician group uses a different patient portal login than the hospital system.
findings.implication: A modern, unified identity provider is a prerequisite for the planned FHIR-based interoperability phase, not a parallel workstream.

findings.theme: Analytics team has partial visibility into patient-access data
findings.evidence: Northstar's analytics team can report on hospital-site access metrics but not ambulatory or physician-group activity.
findings.implication: Care Access Modernization's success metrics need a data-mapping pass before they can be trusted system-wide.

items.title: PHI stays minimal and purpose-bound
items.detail: Every system touching consent or identity data collects only what the specific workflow needs, and nothing is retained past its documented purpose.

items.title: One consent record, everywhere
items.detail: No site-specific consent workaround survives this program — every touchpoint reads and writes the same record.

items.title: Design for FHIR from day one
items.detail: Even before the interoperability phase begins, identity and consent data models are shaped to map cleanly onto FHIR R4 resources.

items.title: Clinical and patient-safety impact gets escalated, not absorbed
items.detail: Any finding that could affect clinical workflow or patient safety goes to governance immediately, not folded into a routine status update.

items.title: PHI never leaves approved systems
items.detail: No consent or identity data is copied into chat, email, or a shared drive outside Northstar's approved systems, even for troubleshooting.

items.title: Decisions are logged, not just discussed
items.detail: Every decision with compliance or clinical impact is recorded in the decision log within one business day of being made.

items.title: Blockers are raised the same day
items.detail: A blocker affecting the consent record or identity integration is raised in the working team channel the day it's found, not saved for the weekly sync.

items.title: Patients see one consistent experience
items.detail: Regardless of which Northstar site a patient visits, the consent and identity experience looks and behaves the same.

items.title: Staff are never asked to work around the system
items.detail: If a front-desk workaround becomes necessary, that's a design defect to fix, not a process to document.
